1

Details

Reach = X17/IPC a 50-day run detects at 3σ (Asimov θ histogram, no TOF). E* ≤ 22 MeV and all E* agree for the Li family: every neutron is ≤ 2.3 MeV.

Birmingham engine value 3.3×10⁻⁴ (full-room Geant4 5.5×10⁻⁴). FRANZ design 3.3×10⁻⁴.

Files: saraf/FEASIBILITY.md, saraf/FACILITY.md, saraf/saraf_beam.py.

The machine: a CW SC proton/deuteron linac in the middle of a rebuild

sources: Mardor EPJA 2018; Tessler PLB 2015; M. Paul 2021; Pichoff LINAC 2024; Bazin LCWS 2025

SARAF
Phase I (2010 – ~2019)p ≤ 4 MeV, 1–2 mA CW (≤ 4 kW); d ≤ 5 MeV. Replaced.
LiLiT1.5 mm liquid-Li jet, ran 1–2 mA at 1.92 MeV, 3–5×10¹⁰ n/s (measured)
⁸Be γ at LiLiT7×10⁸ γ/s/mA, 17.6 + 14.6 MeV (measured): the Birmingham stand-in confirmed
Phase IIp 1.3–35 MeV, d 2.6–40 MeV, 5 mA CW, GaIn 200 kW, thermal source, 18 m TOF (planned)

2

Details

The Phase I linac delivered 1 mA at ~4 MeV or 1.5–2 mA at 2 MeV (3–4 kW). Its RFQ and superconducting module are being replaced by the Phase II linac. Since 2022 no report of Phase I beam was found, and the Phase II cryomodule CM1 was still commissioning in October 2025. FACILITY.md §1.

The lever is the proton energy: every LiLiT-family neutron stays in the window

1.925 MeV: 2.5×10¹⁰ n/s/mA, ≤ 129 keV: too few neutrons.

4 MeV: 2.9×10¹² n/s/mA, ≤ 2.3 MeV: ×115 more per mA, still all in the window.

p + Be at 4 MeV: no ⁸Be γ, ~1×10¹² n/s/mA (ENDF extrapolation).

d + Be at 40 MeV: peak at 16 MeV, 2 % of neutrons in the window.

3

Details

Thick-Li MC (franz/bham): model scale set by the measured 2.5×10¹⁰ n/s/mA at 1.925 MeV; at 2.6 MeV it gives 1.07×10¹², Birmingham's facility number is 1.0×10¹².

σ above 3 MeV is flat (ESTIMATE), ⁷Li(p,n₁) not modelled. d+Be at 5 MeV is an extrapolated Serber shape (ESTIMATE). out/saraf_spectra.csv.

Low energy wins; the 40 MeV beam does not, and the extra current is thrown away

Li jet at 4 MeV, 1 mA: 3.4×10⁻⁴ (2.6 d to ATOMKI), statistics-limited.

5 mA on the jet: 1.5×10⁻⁴ (≥ 20 kW, not demonstrated).

d(40), 5 mA: 1.1×10⁻¹ in the window (4.9×10⁻³ all E*); the beam is throttled to 0.05 %.

p+Be above ~5 MeV also DREAM-limited (live ~0.5), so 5 mA is useless at 18 MeV.

4

Details

Li jet: components at 1 mA and 1 m re-weighted through N5/G5/G6; scaled with I and distance². Throttle scanned; never needed for the Li family at ≤ 4 kW at 1 m.

Reproduction first: saraf_beam.py --check returns Birmingham bham_28_2m_pb5 3.32e-4 and FRANZ design 3.31e-4, ratio 1.000.

Near threshold falls short; energy, not current, makes it work

5

Details

The 5 cm Pb option is worse (neutrons attenuate too). LiLiT at ≥ 2 MeV has not been tested: the jet handled 1.92 MeV at up to 4 kW. out/saraf_shield.csv.

Against the others: on paper a tie with Birmingham, in practice no beam

7

For SARAF to be top-3

Three things must be true

1. CM1 delivers 2–5 MeV protons at ≥ 1 mA CW.

2. LiLiT (or a Be converter) is re-installed in a room with ≥ 1 m free at 0°, tested at ≥ 2.6 MeV.

3. External access is possible at all: site rules, ³He, security.

Not settled

• Room, shield, target chamber: no full Geant4 here.

• σ(E_p) above 3 MeV; d+Be 5 MeV (ESTIMATE).

• Whether LiLiT tolerates 4 MeV beam.
